vignettes.freeText: I have estrogen-receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer that has spread to my bones and liver. I had a lumpectomy years ago, and when it came back I was put on letrozole with palbociclib for about two years, then switched to fulvestrant when the scans showed growth. My most recent blood test found an ESR1 mutation and my oncologist says the fulvestrant is no longer holding things. I feel well overall, work part time and walk every day. My liver lesions are measurable on CT. No brain involvement on my last MRI, and I am not pregnant.

I was diagnosed three weeks ago with triple-negative breast cancer, about 4 cm in my left breast with several lymph nodes under my arm involved, stage III. Genetic testing came back with a BRCA1 mutation, which explains my mother and aunt. The PD-L1 test was positive. I have not started any treatment yet; the plan being discussed is chemotherapy with immunotherapy before surgery, and I want to know whether a trial would be a better option. I am healthy otherwise, running and working full time, and I am not pregnant. I would travel anywhere in the country for the right study.

I have HER2-positive, hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer with spread to my lungs, liver and bones. Over the past five years I have been through docetaxel with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, then T-DM1, then trastuzumab deruxtecan, plus letrozole along the way. Two small brain spots were treated with focused radiation last year and have stayed stable on MRI. I am up and about but tire easily and spend part of the afternoon resting. My heart ultrasound has been normal throughout. I am open to early-phase studies; I only ask that they be within a reasonable drive of Phoenix.

Last year I had a lumpectomy for a stage I estrogen-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer followed by three weeks of radiation, and I have been taking anastrozole since. The joint stiffness is a nuisance but I manage, and I still garden and drive. Eight years ago I had papillary thyroid cancer removed and I have been clear since. I am not interested in anything experimental in the first-in-human sense, but I would consider a later-stage study on preventing recurrence or easing the side effects of the hormone pills, as long as it is close to home in Maine.

I am a man with breast cancer, which surprised everyone including me. I had a mastectomy four years ago for an estrogen-positive, HER2-negative tumor and took tamoxifen afterward. A bone scan this spring showed it has come back in my spine and ribs. I carry a BRCA2 mutation. I feel fine apart from some back pain that Tylenol handles, and I am still working as an electrician. I am not sure whether the bone spots count as measurable; nobody has used that word with me.

My triple-negative breast cancer was first treated with chemotherapy (Adriamycin, Cytoxan and Taxol), a mastectomy and radiation in 2022. It returned in my lungs and liver last year. I had carboplatin and gemcitabine first, which worked for about six months, and I am now on sacituzumab govitecan. My PD-L1 test was negative so immunotherapy was not offered. I have HIV that is well controlled on Biktarvy with an undetectable viral load and a good CD4 count. I have never had a brain scan so I do not know about that. I feel good and would travel anywhere for a promising trial.

I am writing for my mother, who is 80. She was just diagnosed with a large estrogen-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer that has grown into the skin and the lymph nodes under her arm. The doctors say it has not spread elsewhere on scans. She has not had any treatment yet. She is frail: she uses a wheelchair outside the house, spends most of the day in bed or her recliner and needs help bathing. She has atrial fibrillation and takes a blood thinner, and her rheumatoid arthritis has been quiet for years. We can only manage appointments near St. Petersburg.

I am 29 and was diagnosed with stage II HER2-positive, hormone-negative breast cancer, a 3 cm lump with one suspicious node, no spread on scans. I am in the middle of chemotherapy before surgery: docetaxel and carboplatin with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, cycle four of six. The lump has already shrunk noticeably. I am doing well, still working from home, and have an IUD so pregnancy is not a concern. Genetic testing was negative. I would like to hear about studies for young women with HER2-positive disease, ideally in the Seattle area.

I had breast cancer four years ago treated with a mastectomy, chemotherapy and radiation in Rapid City. Last month I found a lump along the scar and the biopsy says the cancer is back. They are still doing scans so I do not yet know whether it has spread anywhere, and I honestly do not remember what type it was or which receptors it had; I will try to get my old reports. I am not sure how many treatments I have had altogether. I am willing to travel a good distance since there is not much available locally.

My hormone-positive breast cancer is HER2-low and has spread to my liver, lungs and now my brain. Since the recurrence I have had letrozole with ribociclib, then fulvestrant with alpelisib because of a PIK3CA mutation, then capecitabine, and most recently trastuzumab deruxtecan. Last month an MRI found three new small brain lesions that have not yet been treated; radiation is being scheduled. I get tired easily and rest a good part of the day but I still take care of myself. I had hepatitis C that was cured with Harvoni in 2016. I am interested in phase 1 options in the Philadelphia area.

I was treated for stage II triple-negative breast cancer this past year: pembrolizumab with carboplatin and paclitaxel, then Adriamycin and Cytoxan, then a mastectomy that showed a small amount of cancer left behind, then radiation. I am now finishing the remaining pembrolizumab infusions. My PD-L1 was positive and the BRCA test was negative. I feel strong and have gone back to work. I am currently enrolled in a survivorship study at my cancer center that tracks exercise and fatigue. I am not pregnant and do not plan to be.

I have stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with an EGFR exon 19 deletion, spread to the bones and the other lung. I have been on osimertinib for fourteen months and my last CT shows the main tumor and a liver spot growing again. Two brain metastases were treated with stereotactic radiation at diagnosis and have been stable since. The full gene panel was otherwise negative, PD-L1 was under 1 percent. I feel well, play golf twice a week and have no other health problems. I live near the Texas Medical Center and would like to know about options after osimertinib.

I am a 41-year-old never-smoker with ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma, stage IV with spread to the liver and bones. Alectinib kept things quiet for almost three years, and I have been on lorlatinib for the past year. My latest brain MRI shows two new small lesions that have not been treated yet, and my oncologist is talking about radiation. Otherwise I feel normal, I work full time and hike on weekends. I am not pregnant. I would fly anywhere for a next-generation ALK trial, including phase 1.

I am a retired farmer with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma, KRAS G12C, PD-L1 around 60 percent. I had carboplatin, pemetrexed and pembrolizumab for about nine months before the cancer grew, and I have been on sotorasib since January; the last scan showed the adrenal spot getting bigger. I get short of breath walking across the yard and spend a fair amount of the day sitting, but I take care of myself. My kidneys are weak from years of diabetes, with a creatinine around 1.8. No brain spots on my scans. I can drive about an hour from Salina.

I had a lobectomy in February for a stage IIB squamous cell lung cancer, then four rounds of cisplatin and vinorelbine, and I am now getting pembrolizumab every six weeks to lower the chance of it coming back. PD-L1 was 55 percent; EGFR and ALK were negative and I do not think the other genes were tested. I smoked for thirty-five years and quit at diagnosis, and I have mild COPD. I have psoriasis that has been clear for years without medication. I feel pretty good and am back to light work. I do not know if I was ever tested for hepatitis.

I am 35 and was diagnosed two weeks ago with lung adenocarcinoma after months of a cough that would not go away. It has spread to lymph nodes in my chest and to a few spots on my bones, so stage IV. The molecular panel found a ROS1 fusion; everything else, including PD-L1, was negative. My brain MRI was clear. I have not started treatment yet and my oncologist mentioned a pill but also said I should ask about trials. I feel well apart from the cough, I am not pregnant, and I would travel anywhere.

Three years ago I had a lobectomy for a stage IB lung adenocarcinoma and needed no further treatment. This spring the cancer came back in lymph nodes in the middle of my chest; scans show no spread beyond that. Sequencing of the recurrence found a HER2 (ERBB2) exon 20 insertion with PD-L1 of zero. I was treated with carboplatin, pemetrexed and pembrolizumab, but after five cycles the nodes have grown and my doctor is talking about trastuzumab deruxtecan or a trial. I feel good and walk a few miles most days. I have not had a brain MRI recently.

I have non-small cell lung cancer that the pathologist could not classify as either adenocarcinoma or squamous, stage IV in my liver and adrenal gland, with a BRAF V600E mutation. I have been through carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab, then docetaxel with ramucirumab, and now dabrafenib and trametinib, which are starting to fail. Whole-brain radiation two years ago took care of several brain spots and they have not come back. I have congestive heart failure with an ejection fraction around 40 percent and get winded easily, so I rest a lot but still get around the house. I am 77 and cannot travel far from Auburn.

I am asking for my mother, who has lung cancer. They told us it is non-small cell but I do not remember which kind. I know the report mentioned a MET exon 14 skipping mutation because she takes capmatinib for it, and that EGFR and ALK were negative. She had some chemotherapy infusions early on, so I am not sure whether the pill counts as her first or second treatment. I believe the cancer is advanced but I honestly do not know where it has spread or whether her brain has been scanned. She gets around the house and cooks but naps most afternoons and does not go out much. We live in Syracuse and could drive an hour or so.

I live on the Big Island and have stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with a RET fusion, spread to bones and lymph nodes. Because the RET result came back late, I started with carboplatin, pemetrexed and pembrolizumab, then switched to selpercatinib about a year ago; my last scan shows a new growing spot in the liver. I have chronic hepatitis B that is controlled on entecavir with an undetectable viral load. No brain metastases on MRI. I feel well, still working as a school custodian, and I am willing to fly to Honolulu or the mainland for a trial.

My husband has extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with spread to the liver and bones. He had four cycles of carboplatin, etoposide and atezolizumab and then maintenance atezolizumab, but the cancer came back five months after the chemo ended. Several brain metastases were treated with whole-brain radiation and have been stable. He has declined a lot in the past month: he is in bed or his chair most of the day and needs help getting to the bathroom. No gene testing was done because they said it is not useful for small cell. His oncologist mentioned lurbinectedin or tarlatamab. We are near Bowling Green and could travel to Nashville or Louisville.

I worked in the Norfolk shipyards for thirty years around asbestos, and last month a biopsy of fluid around my right lung showed epithelioid pleural mesothelioma. The scans show it confined to the lining of that lung with no spread to lymph nodes or elsewhere. I have not started treatment; I meet the thoracic oncologist next week to talk about chemotherapy or immunotherapy. I feel fairly well, a bit short of breath on stairs since they drained the fluid. Six years ago I had prostate cancer treated with radiation and my PSA has stayed down. I would rather stay close to home in Virginia Beach.

I was diagnosed in the spring with sigmoid colon cancer that had already spread to my liver. The surgeon removed the colon tumor because it was nearly blocking me, and I have since had eight cycles of FOLFOX with bevacizumab. The liver spots shrank at first but the latest scan shows two of them growing. The tumor has a KRAS G12D mutation and is microsatellite stable, HER2 and BRAF negative. I feel good, work full time in Dallas and have no other medical problems. I would like to know what trials exist for someone like me before moving to the next chemotherapy.

I have stage III rectal cancer, T3 with a couple of involved lymph nodes, no distant spread. I finished five days of short-course radiation and I am now in the middle of FOLFOX chemotherapy, with surgery planned afterward, though my team mentioned I might avoid surgery if the tumor disappears completely. The tumor was mismatch-repair proficient. I am doing well, still working, and not pregnant. I am in Boston and would be interested in later-phase studies that could spare me the operation or a permanent bag.

My colon cancer was removed four years ago but has since spread to my lungs and the lining of my abdomen. I have had FOLFOX with bevacizumab, then FOLFIRI with cetuximab since my tumor is RAS and BRAF wild type, and for the last few months trifluridine-tipiracil with bevacizumab, which is no longer working. I had a kidney transplant twelve years ago and take tacrolimus; my creatinine runs around 1.9. I get tired and spend about half the day resting but I still manage my own care. I am open to phase 1 studies in Gainesville or nearby.

I was just diagnosed with cancer of the right side of my colon with several spots in my liver. The biopsy shows the tumor is mismatch-repair deficient (MSI-high), which the doctor said matters for immunotherapy. I had endometrial cancer nine years ago treated with a hysterectomy, and they now think I have Lynch syndrome. I have not started any treatment. I do not know the KRAS or BRAF results, and nobody has scanned my head. I feel fine and keep busy on our place outside Hastings, Nebraska; we would drive to Omaha, Kansas City or Denver.

I have squamous cell cancer of the anal canal with spread to lymph nodes in my groin, stage IIIB. I am three weeks into chemoradiation with 5-FU and mitomycin, and the skin burns are rough but I am getting through it. I am HIV positive, diagnosed in 2011, on dolutegravir and undetectable with a CD4 count around 600. No gene testing was done on my tumor. I feel okay and still work from home. I live in Miami and need treatment within a short drive.

I had a right hemicolectomy ten months ago for a stage II colon cancer that was found during a colonoscopy for my ulcerative colitis. The tumor was MSI-high with a BRAF V600E mutation, KRAS normal. Because of some high-risk features I am taking capecitabine, cycle six of eight. My colitis is flaring a little and I am on mesalamine and a short steroid course. Otherwise I feel well and walk every morning. I am in Athens, Ohio, and would drive to Columbus for a study aimed at keeping the cancer from coming back.

I was 36 when I was diagnosed with stage III rectal cancer. I had chemoradiation, surgery with a temporary ileostomy that was later reversed, and FOLFOX afterward. Fourteen months later it recurred in my liver and lungs. I am now on FOLFIRI with bevacizumab, which has kept things stable for seven months but my CEA is creeping up. KRAS G12V mutation, microsatellite stable. I am in excellent shape otherwise and still cycling to work in Manhattan. No brain spots. I would go anywhere for a KRAS-targeted or early-phase study.

I am filling this in for my wife, who is 78 and has colorectal cancer. The surgeon removed part of her large intestine two years ago and she had chemotherapy pills afterward; this summer they told us it has come back, but I am not sure where it started or where it has gone now. I could not tell you which gene tests were done. She has gotten quite weak, uses a walker, and is in bed or lying down most of the day; I help her with washing and dressing. She has a heart valve problem and I am not certain what else is on her chart. We live in Durango and cannot travel far.

I have metastatic colon cancer in my liver and lungs, originally from the left side of the colon, which was resected. First-line FOLFOX with bevacizumab stopped working after about ten months. My tumor is HER2-amplified, RAS and BRAF wild type and microsatellite stable, so for the past four months I have been taking tucatinib with trastuzumab, and it has been working so far. I have chronic hepatitis B controlled on tenofovir. I feel well and surf on weekends. I am in San Diego and could drive to Los Angeles for a trial.

I am 33 and a colonoscopy for rectal bleeding found a cancer in my descending colon last week. The CT scan shows nothing in the liver or lungs and no obviously enlarged nodes, so they are calling it early stage until surgery tells us more. The biopsy showed the mismatch-repair proteins were intact; no other gene tests have been done. Surgery is scheduled in two weeks and I have had no treatment yet. I am healthy, not pregnant, and work as a nurse in Portland. I want to know if there are studies for young people with colon cancer, including ones on preventing recurrence.

I have colon cancer with spread to my liver, diagnosed a year ago in Missoula. The primary tumor was removed, and since the cancer is MSI-high I have been on pembrolizumab as my only treatment. The liver spots shrank for eight months but the latest scan shows one of them growing again. KRAS and BRAF were normal. I feel well, still fish and split my own wood. No brain spots on my scans. My wife and I are willing to fly anywhere for the right trial.

I have prostate cancer that spread to my bones, diagnosed three years ago. I started on leuprolide with abiraterone, which worked for about two years before my PSA started climbing while my testosterone stayed low, so the doctors call it castration resistant. I then had six cycles of docetaxel; my PSA is rising again at 48. Genetic testing of the tumor and my blood showed no BRCA or other repair mutations and the tumor is not MSI-high. The disease is only in bone, nothing measurable on CT. I feel well, walk a couple of miles a day and live near Baltimore.

Two weeks ago I was diagnosed with prostate cancer, Gleason 4+5, with a PSA of 140 and spread to several bones and lymph nodes in my pelvis and abdomen on the PSMA PET scan. I have not had any treatment yet; the urologist wants to start hormone shots next week and refer me to oncology. Genetic testing has been sent but is not back. I feel fine, just some hip ache, and I farm full time outside Ames. I am hormone sensitive at this point as I understand it, and I would travel anywhere for a strong first-line trial.

I was diagnosed last month with high-risk prostate cancer confined to the prostate: Gleason 9, PSA 22, and the PSMA PET showed no spread. I carry a germline BRCA2 mutation; my sister had breast cancer and my father died of prostate cancer. I have not started treatment and am deciding between surgery and radiation with hormone therapy. I am healthy, run three times a week and work as an engineer in New Haven. I do not know whether my tumor counts as measurable. I would travel anywhere for a later-phase trial for BRCA carriers with localized disease.

I had my prostate removed six years ago for Gleason 7 cancer. Last year my PSA began rising again, 0.6 and climbing, with nothing visible on the scans, so I had salvage radiation to the prostate bed along with six months of hormone injections, which I finished in March. My PSA is now 0.1 and we are watching it. Seven years ago I had a melanoma cut off my shoulder with clear margins and no recurrence. I am 76, active, and play tennis. I would only consider something near Greenville.

I am 82 with castration-resistant prostate cancer in my bones and liver. Over eight years I have had leuprolide, enzalutamide, docetaxel, cabazitaxel and six doses of lutetium PSMA, plus radiation to a painful spot in my hip. The liver lesions are growing again and my PSA is over 300. BRCA testing was negative; I am not sure whether MSI was checked. My kidneys are weaker than they should be, which my doctor said may limit some drugs. I am tired and rest much of the day but still get around with a cane. I live in Huntsville and cannot travel far, but I would try a phase 1 study if one were local.

My metastatic prostate cancer, in bones and pelvic lymph nodes, became castration resistant after about two years on leuprolide and apalutamide. Tumor sequencing found a BRCA2 mutation, so I have been on olaparib for the last eleven months; my PSA has started climbing again and a node is larger. I have never had chemotherapy. I had hepatitis C from a transfusion in the 1980s that was cured with antiviral pills in 2015 and my liver tests are normal. I feel well and hike around Reno. I would travel to California or Utah for a trial.

I am 54 and was diagnosed in the winter with prostate cancer that had spread to lymph nodes in my pelvis but nowhere else, stage IVA. I am on leuprolide and abiraterone with prednisone, and I finished radiation to the prostate and pelvic nodes in June; my PSA is now undetectable. Germline testing was negative for BRCA. I have Crohn's disease that is currently active and I take ustekinumab for it. I feel well and work full time in Fayetteville. I would be interested in later-phase studies on intensifying or shortening hormone therapy.

I am filling this out for my husband, who is 79 and has had prostate cancer for several years. He gets a hormone shot every three months and had radiation a while back, and I think he has taken other pills for it too, but I could not tell you the names or how many different treatments he has had. The doctor mentioned his bones once, but I do not know exactly where it has spread or whether it is growing right now. He has become very weak this year, is in bed most of the day and needs help to get up. He also has heart failure and kidney trouble. We are in Alexandria, Louisiana and cannot go far.

I had a prostatectomy at 42 for Gleason 9 cancer. Three years later it came back in my spine and ribs, and I have been on leuprolide plus enzalutamide since. Over the past few months my PSA has risen from 0.4 to 9 despite a castrate testosterone level, so I am now considered castration resistant. Tumor testing showed the cancer is mismatch-repair deficient (MSI-high), which my oncologist says is unusual and might open the door to immunotherapy; BRCA was negative. The disease is in bone only, nothing measurable on CT. I am 47, fit, and work as a firefighter in Columbus; I would go anywhere.

I was diagnosed eight months ago with prostate cancer that had spread to three spots in my bones, so-called low-volume metastatic disease. I am on leuprolide and darolutamide and my PSA has dropped to 0.2; the cancer is still hormone sensitive. I have HIV, well controlled for fifteen years on a single-pill regimen with an undetectable viral load. No genetic testing has been done yet. I feel good and work full time in Durham. I am interested in trials that add something to hormone therapy while it is still working.

I am 85 and have been on active surveillance for a low-grade prostate cancer for four years. My latest biopsy upgraded it to Gleason 3+4 and my PSA is 11, and the scans show it has not spread outside the prostate. I have had no treatment so far and my urologist is now suggesting radiation or hormone therapy. I have coronary artery disease with a pacemaker and I tire easily, so I spend a good part of the day sitting, but I still cook and walk to the mailbox with my cane. I do not know whether I have had any genetic testing. I live in La Crosse and could manage trips to Madison or Rochester.

I was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia last year with FLT3-ITD and NPM1 mutations. I went into remission after 7+3 induction with midostaurin and had two rounds of consolidation, but a bone marrow biopsy nine months later showed the leukemia was back. I started gilteritinib three weeks ago and my counts are starting to recover. We were being worked up for a stem cell transplant before the relapse and that is still on the table. I feel reasonably well, walking and doing light chores. I live near Cleveland and could travel a few hundred miles.

I am 74 and was told last week that I have acute myeloid leukemia after blood work for fatigue and bruising showed very low counts and blasts. The marrow test found an IDH2 mutation; FLT3, NPM1 and TP53 were normal. My doctor says I am not a candidate for strong chemotherapy because of my age and my heart (atrial fibrillation and a weak pump), and plans azacitidine with venetoclax starting next week. I have not had any treatment yet. I am up and about but worn out, resting much of the afternoon. I am in State College and could get to Hershey or Pittsburgh.

I am a 24-year-old graduate student diagnosed four months ago with Philadelphia-chromosome-positive B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. I am being treated with hyper-CVAD chemotherapy together with dasatinib and I am in remission with measurable residual disease still slightly positive. My team is searching for a donor for an allogeneic transplant; my brother is being tested. I feel pretty good between cycles and keep up with coursework. I would go anywhere in the country for a trial that might improve my odds, including newer antibody or CAR-T approaches.

I have Philadelphia-negative B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, first diagnosed at 28. I relapsed after pediatric-style chemotherapy, got into remission with blinatumomab, and had a matched unrelated donor stem cell transplant eighteen months ago. Last month my marrow showed the leukemia is back, about 15 percent blasts, CD19 and CD22 still expressed. I have mild chronic skin graft-versus-host disease controlled with a topical steroid and no longer take immunosuppressants. I feel well and am working part time. I am not pregnant. I would travel anywhere for CAR-T or an early-phase study.

I am 81 with chronic lymphocytic leukemia with a 17p deletion and TP53 mutation. I took ibrutinib for about three years until it had to be stopped for atrial fibrillation and bleeding, then had venetoclax with obinutuzumab, which worked for two years. Now my lymphocyte count and lymph nodes are climbing again and I am anemic. I still live on my own in Bloomington but I tire quickly and sit much of the day. My heart doctor manages the afib with a blood thinner. I would like something I can get locally.

My chronic lymphocytic leukemia was found on routine blood work three years ago and has been on watch-and-wait, but my white count has doubled in the last six months, my spleen is enlarged and I am getting night sweats, so my hematologist says it is time to start treatment. I have never been treated for the CLL. Testing showed no TP53 abnormality and IGHV was unmutated. Twelve years ago I had early breast cancer treated with a lumpectomy and radiation with no recurrence. Two years ago I had an episode of immune thrombocytopenia from the CLL that responded to steroids and has been quiet since. I feel well and hike around Flagstaff; I prefer later-phase trials.

I have had chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia for nine years. Imatinib stopped working after four years, dasatinib had to be stopped because of fluid around my lungs, and nilotinib worked for a while until my BCR-ABL level rose again; the mutation test now shows T315I. My doctor is suggesting asciminib or ponatinib but also mentioned trials. I feel normal, work as an offshore supply coordinator in Lafayette, and have no other health issues. I can drive to New Orleans or Houston.

I went to urgent care last week for feeling full and tired and my white count was 180,000. The hematologist confirmed chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase, BCR-ABL positive, and wants me to start a TKI pill next week; I have not taken anything yet. I am 45, otherwise healthy, not pregnant and had my tubes tied. I do not remember being tested for hepatitis. I live in Camden, New Jersey, and would go into Philadelphia for a study comparing first-line pills.

I have higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome with a TP53 mutation and a complex karyotype, diagnosed last fall. I have had six cycles of azacitidine and my counts have not improved; I need a red cell transfusion every two weeks and my platelets stay low. The marrow still shows about 8 percent blasts. I am 77 with chronic kidney disease, stage 3, and I get tired easily, resting a good part of the day, though I still drive to my appointments. I am not a transplant candidate. I live in Coeur d'Alene and could go to Spokane, including for a phase 1 study.

I am writing for my father, who is 84 and has leukemia. I believe it is one of the chronic kinds, but I am not certain, and I do not know what the gene tests showed. He took pills for it for a couple of years and they worked, but his doctor recently said the leukemia has come back and the pills are no longer holding it. I am not sure how many different treatments he has had. He is very weak now, in bed most of the day, and needs help to walk to the bathroom. He has several other health problems I cannot list from memory. We are in Hattiesburg and he cannot travel far.

I was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia five months ago, NPM1-mutated and FLT3-negative. Because of my heart history and HIV my doctors chose azacitidine with venetoclax rather than intensive chemotherapy, and I am in remission after cycle four, though the NPM1 level in my blood is still detectable. My HIV has been undetectable for twenty years on antiretrovirals. Six years ago I had early-stage breast cancer treated with surgery and radiation. I am enrolled in a symptom-tracking app study at my cancer center. I feel well and am 59, postmenopausal and not pregnant. I live in Worcester and would travel to New York or Baltimore.

I have diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, first diagnosed two years ago. I got six cycles of R-CHOP and went into remission, but it came back about eight months later, so I had CAR-T cell therapy (axi-cel) in the spring. The latest PET scan shows new active nodes in my abdomen and neck, so the CAR-T did not hold. I still feel reasonably well, I drive myself to appointments and do my own yard work. I am in Columbus, Ohio and would travel a couple of hours for the right study.

I was diagnosed with grade 2 follicular lymphoma, stage III, about four years ago and was on watch-and-wait for a while. Last year I was treated with bendamustine plus rituximab and then rituximab maintenance, which we stopped a few months ago when scans showed it was growing again in my groin and chest nodes. I have Hashimoto's thyroiditis on levothyroxine but no other autoimmune problems. I feel fine day to day and work full time. We live in Missoula, Montana, so most big centers are a flight away, but I am willing to go to Seattle or Denver for a later-phase trial.

My father has mantle cell lymphoma, diagnosed seven years ago. He had R-hyper-CVAD followed by an autologous stem cell transplant, then rituximab maintenance, then ibrutinib for about three years until it stopped working, and most recently venetoclax with rituximab, which also failed. His TP53 mutation was found on the last biopsy. He has atrial fibrillation and a reduced heart pump function (ejection fraction around 40%), which his doctors watch closely. He is tired and rests a good part of the day but still gets around the house. He lives in Miami Beach and does not want to travel far, and we are open to early-phase studies since standard options are running out.

I was just diagnosed with nodal marginal zone lymphoma after a lymph node biopsy from my armpit; the PET shows disease on both sides of my diaphragm. I have not had any treatment yet, and my hematologist wants to start something in the next month or two. I have chronic hepatitis C that was never treated; my liver numbers are normal and she says it may be related to the lymphoma. I am healthy otherwise, I am not pregnant, and I run three times a week. I live in Portland, Maine and would travel to Boston or beyond for a trial.

I am 27 and have classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis type, stage IIB when I was diagnosed. I did six cycles of ABVD and radiation to my chest and was in remission for about a year. It came back in my neck and mediastinum, and I just finished brentuximab vedotin plus nivolumab as second-line, which shrank things but did not clear them on PET. My team is talking about a transplant versus a trial. I feel completely normal, I am back at the gym, and I will go anywhere in the country for the best option.

I have peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified, found in March. I am in the middle of CHOEP chemotherapy right now, cycle four of six, and the midway scan looked somewhat better but my doctor is already talking about what comes next because this type tends to come back. I had prostate cancer treated with surgery nine years ago with no recurrence. My kidneys are a bit weak (stage 3 chronic kidney disease) from years of high blood pressure. I honestly do not know how my doctor would rate my activity level; some days I am fine and some days chemo knocks me down. I live in Omaha and could travel to Chicago or Kansas City if needed.

I am writing for my mother, who is 80 and has non-Hodgkin lymphoma that has come back. I do not know the exact subtype; the doctor said it is a B-cell type and she has had a few rounds of chemo with an antibody infusion over the past several years, but I am not sure how many different regimens. She has congestive heart failure and kidney problems, is mostly in a chair or bed now, and needs help bathing and dressing. She lives in Greenville, South Carolina and really cannot travel more than a short drive. We would only consider something gentle and well established, not an experimental first-in-human study.

I am a 45-year-old woman with relapsed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (germinal center type, double-hit on FISH). I have been through R-CHOP, then R-ICE and an autologous transplant, then glofitamab, and after that relapse I had a reduced-intensity allogeneic transplant from my brother about 14 months ago. I am currently in a phase 2 study of a new antibody, but my last scan showed progression so I will be coming off it. I also have HIV that has been undetectable on Biktarvy for over a decade with a normal CD4 count. I feel surprisingly good, walking several miles a day, and I am in Seattle and able to drive to Portland or fly within the Northwest. I am not pregnant and have an IUD.

I was diagnosed with IgG kappa multiple myeloma three weeks ago after my kidney function dropped and I had a compression fracture in my spine. Bone marrow showed 60% plasma cells and the FISH report mentions gain of 1q. I have not started any treatment yet; my doctor in Atlanta is proposing a four-drug combination with daratumumab and then possibly a transplant. My creatinine is about 2.0 and improving with fluids. Apart from back pain that is controlled with medication I am active and still working part time. I would rather be in a larger, later-stage study than something very early.

I have had multiple myeloma for nine years. I started with bortezomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone, had an autologous stem cell transplant, and stayed on lenalidomide maintenance for a few years. When it relapsed I was given daratumumab with pomalidomide, and after that carfilzomib with cyclophosphamide. My M-spike is climbing again and my light chains are rising, and I am now considered triple-class refractory. I have peripheral neuropathy in my feet from the bortezomib and tire easily, so I spend part of the afternoon resting, but I cook and get out of the house most days. I live in Providence and could go to Boston or New Haven for a trial, and I am open to CAR-T or bispecific studies.

I have smoldering multiple myeloma, found by chance on blood work about 18 months ago. My bone marrow had 15% plasma cells and my M-protein is around 2.5 g/dL, and my hematologist calls it high-risk smoldering because of the free light chain ratio. I have no bone lesions, normal calcium and kidneys, and no symptoms; we are on a watch-and-wait plan with labs every three months. I had early-stage breast cancer six years ago treated with lumpectomy and radiation and have been clear since. I am 55, not pregnant (I had a hysterectomy), and in excellent shape. I am in Phoenix and would travel to California or Texas for a prevention or early-intervention study.

My doctor found an abnormal protein in my blood and I was told I have MGUS, a precursor condition to myeloma, with an IgA M-spike of 1.1 g/dL. I have had no treatment and do not need any right now; we just recheck labs every six months. I also have rheumatoid arthritis that flares a few times a year and I take methotrexate and occasionally prednisone for it. I work full time as an electrician in Detroit and feel fine. I am interested in studies that follow people like me or try to keep MGUS from progressing, but only something close to home.

I have AL amyloidosis with lambda light chains, diagnosed in January after months of swelling in my legs and shortness of breath. It has affected my heart (Mayo stage III, NT-proBNP in the thousands) and my kidneys, with a lot of protein in my urine. I am currently on daratumumab plus bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone, about five months in, and my light chains have come down but not to where the doctors want. I get winded climbing stairs and spend a fair amount of the day sitting, though I can take care of myself. I live in Nashville and could travel to a center within a couple of hours.

I am 38 and was diagnosed with multiple myeloma at 35 after a plasmacytoma in my pelvis that needed radiation. My FISH showed t(4;14) and deletion 17p, so I was considered high risk from the start. I had daratumumab-VRd induction, a stem cell transplant, and lenalidomide maintenance, but it relapsed within a year with new bone lesions and a rising M-spike. I just finished a second regimen of carfilzomib, pomalidomide and dexamethasone and my markers are rising again. I feel strong and active, hike on weekends, and am definitely not pregnant. I live in Santa Fe and will travel anywhere in the US, including for first-in-human or CAR-T trials.

My husband is 78 and has myeloma. He has been on some kind of pill chemotherapy and a weekly shot at the cancer clinic in Cedar Rapids for the past couple of years, but I could not tell you the names or how many different treatments he has had. The doctor recently said the numbers are drifting up and we may need to change course. He has never had a transplant. I am not sure how the doctors would rate his energy; he is slower than he used to be but still drives and goes to church. We do not know much about his other health details offhand but can bring his records. We would stay within an hour or so of home and prefer established treatments.

I am a 59-year-old man with heavily pretreated multiple myeloma, diagnosed at 51. I have had five lines: VRd with an autologous transplant, daratumumab-pomalidomide, carfilzomib-based therapy, cilta-cel CAR-T (which gave me almost two years), and then teclistamab, a BCMA bispecific, which stopped working this summer. After the CAR-T relapse I also had an allogeneic transplant from an unrelated donor as part of a research protocol, and I am still enrolled in that study's follow-up. I carry chronic hepatitis B and take entecavir, with undetectable viral load. I feel good for all that, walking daily and working from home. I am in Houston near the medical center and would travel across Texas or to nearby states for a novel-mechanism phase 1 trial.

I had a melanoma removed from my back three years ago (stage IIB), and this spring scans found spots in my lungs and liver, so I am now stage IV. The tumor carries a BRAF V600E mutation. I started ipilimumab plus nivolumab as first-line treatment two months ago and have had two doses; the first restaging scan is coming up and my doctor wants a backup plan. A brain MRI was clear. I feel well, I am back to cycling on weekends and working full time in Denver. I would drive a couple of hours for a good study.

I am 69 with metastatic cutaneous melanoma, BRAF wild-type and PD-L1 positive. After the primary on my leg was removed and lymph nodes were involved, I had a year of adjuvant pembrolizumab, then relapsed in the lungs and a single spot in the brain, which was treated with Gamma Knife radiosurgery and has been stable on MRI for ten months. My second-line treatment was nivolumab plus relatlimab, and now the lung spots are growing again. The immunotherapy gave me colitis that is still being managed with a low dose of budesonide, which my oncologist considers an active autoimmune-type issue. I am otherwise independent and active in Tampa, and I would prefer a phase 2 or 3 trial within an hour of home.

I was treated for uveal melanoma in my left eye with plaque brachytherapy five years ago. Routine liver imaging this summer showed multiple liver metastases, confirmed by biopsy, and I am told the tumor is HLA-A*02:01 negative so tebentafusp is not an option for me. I have not had any systemic treatment yet for the metastatic disease; nothing was tested for BRAF or PD-L1 since my oncologist says it does not usually matter in uveal melanoma. I feel completely well and work full time in Madison, Wisconsin. I am willing to travel to Chicago, the Twin Cities or further for liver-directed or novel therapies.

My mother, 74, has mucosal melanoma of the sinonasal cavity. She had surgery and radiation two years ago, and it recurred in the neck lymph nodes last year, for which she received about ten months of pembrolizumab before the nodes started growing again. Molecular testing showed no BRAF mutation but a KIT mutation, and PD-L1 was negative. She lives in Honolulu, tires easily and naps in the afternoons, but manages her own cooking and errands. Because options at home are so limited we are prepared to fly her anywhere on the mainland for a trial.

I am an 82-year-old man and I had a kidney transplant 15 years ago; I still take tacrolimus and mycophenolate. Over the years I have had many skin cancers removed, and a squamous cell carcinoma on my scalp came back after surgery and radiation and has now spread to lung nodules. My oncologist tried cemiplimab for a few months with careful monitoring of the transplant, but the lung spots grew. The tumor was PD-L1 high. I have never had a brain scan so I do not know about that. I also had a small bladder cancer scraped out eight years ago that never came back. My transplanted kidney works at about 45%. I get around with a cane and tire easily. I live in Little Rock and could travel to Memphis or Dallas.

I had a Merkel cell carcinoma on my forearm that was removed last fall along with a positive sentinel lymph node, stage III. After the lymph node dissection I had radiation to the area, and I am now partway through a year of adjuvant avelumab infusions; there is currently no measurable cancer on my scans. I do not know whether they tested the tumor for PD-L1 or anything else. I have a pacemaker and coronary stents but my cardiologist says I am stable. I split wood and walk the dog every day. I live in Bangor, Maine, and would travel to Boston for a study aimed at keeping this from coming back.

I have a locally advanced basal cell carcinoma on the side of my face that has invaded toward the orbit and parotid area. It was cut out twice over the years, then radiated, and when it came back again I was put on vismodegib for about a year and then sonidegib; both worked for a while but I could not tolerate the muscle cramps and the tumor has started growing again. No one has tested it for PD-L1. I have HIV that is fully suppressed on dolutegravir/lamivudine with a CD4 over 600. I am otherwise fit and work as a casino dealer in Las Vegas, and I would like to stay local for treatment.

I am a 34-year-old woman with stage IV BRAF V600K melanoma that has spread to my liver, bones and brain. I have been through ipilimumab plus nivolumab, then dabrafenib and trametinib for about a year, then encorafenib with binimetinib briefly, plus whole-brain radiation last month because several new brain lesions appeared and some are still growing. My liver enzymes are elevated from the metastases and I am now mostly in bed, needing help from my partner for most things. PD-L1 was negative. I am not pregnant. We are in Minneapolis but would travel fairly far for an early-phase trial that accepts active brain metastases, understanding that few will.

I have pancreatic adenocarcinoma in the head of the pancreas with several liver metastases, diagnosed in April. I am on first-line FOLFIRINOX, eight cycles in, and the last CT showed the liver spots are stable but my CA 19-9 is starting to rise. Genomic testing found a KRAS G12D mutation; BRCA1/2 and PALB2 were negative and the tumor is microsatellite stable. I have a biliary stent that is working fine. I feel pretty good between cycles, walk a few miles a day and still handle my own business from home. I live in Philadelphia and could travel to New York or Baltimore for a trial when this chemo stops working.

I was just told I have pancreatic cancer, adenocarcinoma, in the body of the pancreas, about 3.5 cm, touching the superior mesenteric vein. The surgeon calls it borderline resectable and wants me to have chemotherapy first before deciding on surgery. I have had no treatment yet and no molecular testing has come back. I am 71 but active, still gardening and driving, with mild type 2 diabetes that is new this year. I live in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, and am willing to travel to Minneapolis, Omaha or Rochester for a trial of treatment before surgery.

I have a well-differentiated grade 2 pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, non-functional, with liver metastases. I had a distal pancreatectomy four years ago, then was on monthly lanreotide injections for about two years until the liver lesions grew, and I have been on everolimus for the past year, which is now showing slow progression on the latest MRI. Ki-67 was 8%. Genomic testing found no actionable mutations and no BRCA or MSI findings. I feel good and work full time in downtown Los Angeles. I am not pregnant and use contraception. I would like to stay in the LA area and am interested in PRRT or newer targeted options.

I had a Whipple operation in February for a stage IIB pancreatic adenocarcinoma, with two positive lymph nodes and clear margins. I carry a germline BRCA2 mutation (my sister has it too), the tumor has a KRAS mutation, and MSI testing was stable. I am now finishing adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX, cycle 10 of 12, and scans show no evidence of disease. I am a 56-year-old man in Manhattan, back to working and exercising, and I will travel anywhere for a maintenance or recurrence-prevention trial, especially one using a PARP inhibitor or a vaccine.

I have metastatic pancreatic cancer that has spread to the liver and peritoneum, diagnosed almost three years ago, which my doctors say is unusually long. The tumor turned out to be mismatch repair deficient (MSI-high), so after gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel and then FOLFOX, I received pembrolizumab, which worked for about 14 months. Since then I have had radiation to a painful spot in my spine and the cancer is growing again on scans. My bilirubin has been creeping up and I may need a stent. I am tired and spend about half the day resting, but I can still manage my own care. I have never had a brain scan. I live in Louisville and could travel to Cincinnati, Indianapolis or Nashville for a phase 1 trial.

My dad is 79 and has pancreatic cancer. He is getting chemotherapy every other week in Anchorage, and I think he has been on a couple of different combinations over the past year, but I do not have the names or know exactly where the cancer has spread, only that surgery was never an option. I am not aware of any genetic testing results. He had a heart attack six years ago and has stents. He still lives on his own and walks to the store, but he has lost a lot of weight. We are open to flying to Seattle for a trial if it would help.

I am a 44-year-old woman with locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma that wraps around the celiac artery, so it cannot be removed, but there is no spread beyond the pancreas on PET. I have completed six months of FOLFIRINOX and then chemoradiation with capecitabine, and the tumor is stable and my CA 19-9 is normal. Germline testing found a PALB2 mutation; BRCA1 and BRCA2 were negative, KRAS was mutated, and the tumor is microsatellite stable. I feel well, I am back at work as a teacher in Raleigh, and I am not pregnant. I would travel within the Southeast for a maintenance trial, particularly something targeting DNA-repair mutations.

My husband is 75 and had a Whipple for pancreatic cancer two years ago, followed by gemcitabine and capecitabine. It came back in the lungs and liver last year and he had gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel until a few weeks ago, when he became too weak to continue. His tumor was KRAS wild-type, and the doctors mentioned an NRG1 fusion they are looking into. He was also diagnosed with a separate early prostate cancer during this workup, which is being watched. He has chronic hepatitis B on tenofovir, his kidneys are weak and his liver numbers are off. He is in bed or a recliner most of the day and needs help with most activities. We are in Boise and cannot travel more than a short drive; we would only consider a well-established trial, not an early one.

I was diagnosed with stage IIIC high-grade serous ovarian cancer at 54. I had debulking surgery and carboplatin/paclitaxel, then two years of olaparib maintenance because I have a germline BRCA1 mutation. It recurred 20 months after my last platinum with nodules in the liver capsule and lung, so I just finished second-line carboplatin and liposomal doxorubicin with a good partial response, and we are discussing what maintenance to use now that I have already had a PARP inhibitor. I am 58, postmenopausal, and in great shape, running most mornings. I live in Chicago and would travel in the Midwest.

I have high-grade serous ovarian cancer, originally stage IV with pleural fluid, diagnosed five years ago. I have had carboplatin/paclitaxel with bevacizumab, niraparib maintenance (BRCA negative but HRD positive), a platinum rechallenge, then weekly paclitaxel with bevacizumab when I became platinum resistant, and most recently mirvetuximab since my tumor is folate receptor alpha high. I am currently in a phase 2 trial of an experimental antibody-drug conjugate but my CA-125 is rising and the scan next week will probably show progression. My kidneys were damaged by the platinum (creatinine 1.6). I get tired and sit much of the afternoon, but I still cook and drive. I am in Dallas and would travel to Houston or elsewhere in Texas for a phase 1 study.

I am 29 and was just diagnosed with an immature teratoma of the right ovary, a germ cell tumor, after an ultrasound for pelvic pain showed a 12 cm mass. It appears confined to the ovary on CT, and my gynecologic oncologist is planning fertility-sparing surgery in the next two weeks, with chemo possibly after depending on the grade. I have had no treatment yet and no genetic testing. I am not pregnant and we want to preserve fertility if at all possible. I am otherwise completely healthy and live in Portland, Oregon; I would travel a long way for a specialist center or a trial for young women with germ cell tumors.

I have low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, which I understand behaves differently from the common type. I had a hysterectomy and debulking three years ago, followed by carboplatin/paclitaxel, which did very little, and then letrozole for about 18 months, which held it steady until recently. Now there are growing peritoneal and liver surface nodules and I would be considered platinum resistant. Tumor testing showed a KRAS G12V mutation, no BRCA mutation and microsatellite stable. I have celiac disease that is well controlled on a gluten-free diet. I am 51, in menopause after my surgery, and very active. I live in St. Louis and would travel a couple of hours for a MEK inhibitor or other targeted trial.

I am 72 and was diagnosed in the summer with high-grade serous ovarian cancer, stage IIIB, with disease in the pelvis and nearby lymph nodes and omentum but nothing in distant organs. Because of my heart condition (I have had two valve surgeries and atrial fibrillation) the surgeons wanted me to start with chemotherapy first; I am on my third cycle of carboplatin and paclitaxel and interval surgery is being planned. They sent off genetic and HRD testing but I have not heard results yet. I get short of breath and need to rest in the afternoons, but I manage at home with my husband's help. I live in Burlington, Vermont and would not go further than Dartmouth or so, and only for a later-phase trial.

I had a complete debulking surgery for stage IIIA high-grade serous ovarian cancer eight months ago, followed by six cycles of carboplatin/paclitaxel with bevacizumab, and I am now on maintenance bevacizumab plus olaparib with no visible disease on my scans. Unusually, my tumor was found to be MSI-high and mismatch repair deficient; I was also tested for Lynch syndrome and I do carry an MSH2 mutation, which fits because I had colon cancer removed at age 49 with no recurrence. BRCA testing was negative. I feel fine and hike regularly around Salt Lake City. I would travel within the Mountain West for a maintenance or immunotherapy trial.

My grandmother is 84 and has ovarian cancer that has come back. She had an operation and chemotherapy a few years ago in Montgomery and has had more chemo since, but the family does not know the type of ovarian cancer or how many treatments she has been given, and nobody has told us about genetic tests. She has heart failure and kidney disease, is mostly in bed, and needs help with nearly everything now. She cannot go far from home. We are asking about anything close by that is well studied and gentle; she would not want an experimental early-phase treatment.

I am a 40-year-old woman with recurrent high-grade serous ovarian cancer and a germline BRCA2 mutation. Since diagnosis at 35 I have had surgery, carboplatin/paclitaxel, niraparib maintenance, a second platinum doublet, bevacizumab with weekly paclitaxel, and most recently topotecan; my disease is now platinum resistant and spreading in the abdomen and lungs. A single brain metastasis was treated with stereotactic radiation last year and has stayed stable. I have well-controlled HIV on a single-tablet regimen with an undetectable viral load since my twenties. I am not pregnant. I still feel strong, work part time and exercise, and I live in Baltimore but will go anywhere in the country for a first-in-human or novel-combination study.

I was diagnosed with glioblastoma in my right frontal lobe 11 months ago. I had a near-total resection, then six weeks of radiation with temozolomide and six monthly cycles of temozolomide afterward. The tumor is IDH wild-type and MGMT promoter methylated. My MRI last week shows a new enhancing area at the edge of the cavity that my neuro-oncologist believes is true recurrence rather than treatment effect. I am on a low dose of dexamethasone and levetiracetam for seizures, which are controlled. I feel well, walk daily and manage everything on my own. I live in Boston and would drive a couple of hours for a recurrent GBM trial.

My wife, 66, had a seizure three weeks ago and an MRI showed a large tumor in her left temporal lobe. She had surgery to remove most of it, and the pathology came back as glioblastoma, IDH wild-type with an unmethylated MGMT promoter. She has not started radiation or chemotherapy yet; the team in Kansas City wants to begin in about two weeks. She has some word-finding trouble and tires quickly, so she is up and about but not able to do her usual work. There is residual tumor on the post-op scan. We would travel to St. Louis, Chicago or Houston for a newly diagnosed trial, preferably one with some track record rather than first-in-human.

I am 36 and have a grade 3 astrocytoma, IDH1 mutant, 1p/19q intact, MGMT methylated, first found when I was 29. I had two surgeries, radiation with temozolomide after the second, and later a course of PCV when it progressed. The MRI now shows slow regrowth with a new area of enhancement, and my oncologist is talking about vorasidenib or a trial. I feel normal and work full time as a software engineer in San Francisco; my only medication is lamotrigine for seizures. I am not pregnant and have no plans to be during treatment. I would fly anywhere in the western US for an IDH-targeted study.

I had a grade 2 oligodendroglioma removed from my right frontal lobe two months ago, found after headaches and a single seizure. It is IDH mutant with 1p/19q co-deletion; I do not remember whether MGMT was reported. There is a small amount of residual tumor on the follow-up MRI. My doctors say I could watch and wait, go straight to radiation and chemotherapy, or consider a trial, and I would like to understand the trial options before deciding. I am 42, otherwise healthy, working and running in Richmond, Virginia, and would travel to Baltimore, Durham or DC.

I have a recurrent grade 3 (anaplastic) meningioma along the skull base that has now invaded the bone and extended toward the orbit and neck. Over 12 years I have had four surgeries, two courses of radiation including proton therapy, then bevacizumab, then sunitinib, and most recently everolimus with octreotide, all of which eventually failed. The tumor was never tested for IDH or MGMT since those are glioma markers. I had early-stage melanoma excised from my shoulder six years ago with no recurrence. I have double vision and some facial numbness, tire easily and rest much of the afternoon, but I manage my own care. I live in Tucson and would travel for an early-phase study for meningioma.

A 3 cm meningioma was found over my left parietal lobe on an MRI done for dizziness. It has not been biopsied or treated; the neurosurgeon thinks it is probably a grade 1 tumor based on the imaging and we are deciding between observation, radiosurgery and surgery. I am 70 with a history of lupus that has been quiet for years without medication, and I have had a heart stent. I am independent and active, driving and volunteering. I live in Scranton and would go to Philadelphia for a trial, but only a larger, later-phase one.

My brother is 48 and has had glioblastoma for two and a half years, IDH wild-type and MGMT unmethylated, with EGFR amplification. He has had two resections, standard radiation with temozolomide, bevacizumab, lomustine, and then a trial of an experimental immunotherapy that he is technically still enrolled in but has progressed on. The tumor is now growing on both sides across the corpus callosum. He is weak on his right side, needs a wheelchair, and is on 8 mg of dexamethasone a day; he depends on us for most daily care. He lives with us in Jacksonville and we would take him anywhere for a phase 1 trial, though we understand his condition may rule many out.

I am 76 and I have a malignant brain tumor; the biopsy was done in Indianapolis in July and I was told it is a high-grade glioma but I cannot recall the exact name or any of the markers they talked about. I am currently getting radiation treatments every weekday and taking a chemotherapy pill with it. The tumor could not be removed because of where it sits. I am not sure how my doctor would describe my activity level; I need my daughter to drive me and I get confused in the evenings. I cannot travel far and would just like to know what might be available in town.

I had muscle-invasive urothelial bladder cancer treated with neoadjuvant gemcitabine and cisplatin and then a radical cystectomy with an ileal conduit three years ago. Last year it came back in my lungs and retroperitoneal lymph nodes, and I was treated with pembrolizumab for about ten months; the tumor was PD-L1 positive and microsatellite stable. The newest CT shows the lung nodules are growing. My kidney function is reduced (eGFR around 45), so cisplatin is off the table. I am 70, walk a few miles a day and still work part time. I live in Cleveland and would travel to Pittsburgh or Columbus for an antibody-drug conjugate or targeted trial.

I have high-grade non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ. After the first TURBT I completed a full induction course of BCG plus maintenance, but my cystoscopy and biopsies this month show CIS has come back, so my urologist calls it BCG-unresponsive and is raising the question of removing my bladder. I would like to try to keep it. No molecular testing has been done on the tumor. I am 64, in excellent health otherwise, and a former smoker who quit 20 years ago. I live in Hartford, Connecticut and can drive about an hour for a bladder-sparing trial.

I am a 59-year-old woman who had muscle-invasive bladder cancer (urothelial with some squamous features). I had four cycles of dose-dense MVAC before surgery, then a radical cystectomy with a neobladder in May; the pathology still showed residual muscle-invasive tumor and one positive node, so I am now on adjuvant nivolumab, about four months in. There is no visible cancer on my scans right now. The tumor was PD-L1 negative and MSI stable; a panel found an FGFR3 mutation. I am postmenopausal and not pregnant. I feel very well, back to work and swimming, and I live in St. Paul, Minnesota; I would travel in the upper Midwest for an adjuvant or ctDNA-guided later-phase trial.

I have metastatic urothelial carcinoma that started in the renal pelvis rather than the bladder, with spread to bones, liver and one brain lesion that was treated with radiosurgery a year ago and has stayed quiet. The tumor is MSI-high (I have Lynch syndrome and had colon cancer removed 12 years ago), yet pembrolizumab only worked for eight months. Since then I have had gemcitabine/carboplatin, enfortumab vedotin, and erdafitinib for an FGFR3 alteration, and now everything is progressing again, with palliative radiation to my hip last month. I have coronary disease with a reduced ejection fraction. I spend a good part of the day resting but can still get myself around. I live in Albuquerque and would fly to Houston, Denver or Los Angeles for a phase 1 trial.

I am 81 and was found to have bladder cancer after blood in my urine. The urologist scraped out a high-grade tumor that had not gone into the muscle, and he wants to start BCG treatments in a few weeks; nothing else has been done so far. I do not know anything about tumor markers. I have heart failure and my kidneys are weak, and I use a walker and get tired after an hour of being up, though I still live alone with help from my daughter. I am in Erie, Pennsylvania and cannot travel far. I would only consider something well established.

I am a 52-year-old woman just diagnosed with muscle-invasive urothelial bladder cancer; the CT shows the tumor going through the bladder wall and two enlarged pelvic lymph nodes, but no spread beyond that. I have had only the diagnostic TURBT so far and have not started any treatment. My oncologist in New Orleans is proposing chemotherapy before surgery and mentioned trials that add immunotherapy. I had hepatitis C that was cured with Epclusa four years ago, with a normal liver now. I am not pregnant, I am active and work as a nurse. I would travel to Houston or Birmingham for the right pre-surgery trial.

My father, 77, has bladder cancer and gets infusions every few weeks at the cancer center in Birmingham, Alabama. I believe he has had chemotherapy and some type of immunotherapy, maybe in combination, but I do not know the names or how many different treatments he has tried, and I am not certain whether the cancer has spread beyond the bladder. He has one kidney after an operation years ago, and I do not know about any prior cancers for sure. He still drives himself to appointments but his stamina is uncertain. He would stay within about an hour of home.

I am 45 and was diagnosed eight months ago with metastatic urothelial carcinoma of the bladder with liver and lung metastases; PD-L1 was high and the tumor is microsatellite stable. I started first-line enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab and responded well at first, but a brain MRI done for new headaches two weeks ago shows three small lesions that have not been treated yet, and the liver spots are growing. I feel pretty normal apart from the headaches, which are controlled with a short steroid course, and I am still working and exercising. I live in Oklahoma City and will travel anywhere in the country for a trial, including early-phase studies that allow brain metastases.

I was diagnosed three weeks ago with clear cell kidney cancer after a CT scan for back pain found a 9 cm mass on my left kidney. The scan also showed several small spots in both lungs and the biopsy of one of them confirmed it is the same cancer, so they are calling it stage 4. I have not had any treatment yet; the oncologist is talking about starting an immunotherapy combination but said a trial might be an option first. I feel pretty normal, still working full time as an electrician, just some fatigue and the back ache. No other health problems to speak of. Nobody has scanned my head, and I have never been tested for hepatitis that I know of. I do not know enough about trial phases to have a preference.

Clear cell renal cell carcinoma, found in 2022 when I had my right kidney removed. It came back in my lungs and bones about a year later. First I had ipilimumab plus nivolumab, which worked for about 14 months, and I have been on cabozantinib since, but the last scan showed the lung spots growing again. I also had one small brain metastasis treated with focused radiation (Gamma Knife) last spring and it has stayed stable since. I am still active, I walk the dog a couple of miles every day and do my own housework. We live in Montana so we are used to traveling for care and will go wherever we need to.

I have papillary renal cell carcinoma, which I am told is a non-clear-cell type. My kidney was removed in 2023 and I thought I was done. Last year it came back in the lymph nodes behind my abdomen, not anywhere else according to the PET scan. I have been taking cabozantinib for about 8 months and it shrank things at first, but the latest scan shows the nodes are growing again. I feel fine day to day apart from hand-foot soreness and some diarrhea from the pill. I have Hashimoto's thyroid disease that is controlled with levothyroxine. I am not pregnant and we are done having children. I have never been checked for hepatitis as far as I know, and I have no idea which trial phase would suit me.

I had my left kidney taken out in January for a clear cell kidney cancer that was large and had grown into the fat around the kidney, but the scans before and after surgery showed nothing elsewhere. Because it was considered high risk, I have been getting pembrolizumab infusions every six weeks as a preventive treatment, and I have about four months left. I honestly do not know how to count treatment lines since this is the only drug I have had, and only after surgery. I had prostate cancer treated with radiation eight years ago and it has not come back. I am retired, feel well, and still split my own firewood.

I am writing for my mother, who is 81. A scan for blood in her urine found a large tumor in her kidney and the biopsy said renal cell carcinoma, but nobody has told us which type. The doctor mentioned some areas on her spine that could be cancer too, so we do not really know yet whether it has spread. She has not started any treatment. She is frail, mostly in bed or in her chair, and needs help bathing and getting dressed. She also has heart failure and her kidney function is poor. We cannot travel far from Jackson, and we do not know her hepatitis status or much of her older medical history.

I am 35 with metastatic kidney cancer, a translocation (TFE3) type that the doctors say is non-clear-cell and rare for adults. Since 2022 I have been through sunitinib, then nivolumab, then cabozantinib, and I am now on lenvatinib with everolimus, which is my fourth treatment; the disease in my liver and lungs is still slowly growing. I am tired and spend a good part of the day resting, but I am up and about and manage my own care. I have HIV that has been undetectable for ten years on Biktarvy. I am very interested in early-phase trials and will travel anywhere in the country.

I received a kidney transplant in 2014 for polycystic kidney disease, and on a routine ultrasound this month they found a 6 cm tumor in one of my original, non-working kidneys. The biopsy came back as clear cell renal cell carcinoma and the CT scan shows it is confined to that kidney with no spread. Surgery to remove the kidney is planned but my transplant team is worried about my anti-rejection drugs (tacrolimus and mycophenolate) and wants to know about any studies for transplant patients. My transplanted kidney works reasonably well though the creatinine runs a little high. I feel good and work on our ranch most days. I am not sure what counts as measurable disease on a scan.

I have had hepatitis B since childhood and cirrhosis for several years, and my surveillance ultrasound in August picked up a liver tumor. The MRI shows a 7 cm hepatocellular carcinoma with a clot of tumor in a branch of the portal vein and an enlarged lymph node nearby, but no spread outside the liver area, so surgery and transplant are off the table. I have not started any cancer treatment yet; I take entecavir for the hepatitis. My liver is still compensated (Child-Pugh A, my doctor says), I have no fluid in my belly, and I feel well enough to keep working at our family restaurant. Nobody has mentioned any gene tests on the tumor, and I do not know what measurable disease means or which trial phase would be right.

I was diagnosed in March with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, a bile duct cancer inside the liver, with spread to lymph nodes in my abdomen and a few spots in my lungs. Genomic testing found an IDH1 mutation (R132C). I have been getting gemcitabine and cisplatin with durvalumab since April and have had six cycles so far; the last scan was stable. My oncologist mentioned IDH-targeted drugs and trials for when this stops working, and I would like to be ready. I am a schoolteacher, still working part time, with normal energy most days except right after chemo. I am not pregnant. I have never had a brain scan, so I do not know about that, and I have no preference about trial phase.

My hepatocellular carcinoma was first removed by surgery in 2021. It came back in 2023 with several lung metastases and a new liver lesion. I was treated with atezolizumab and bevacizumab for a little over a year, then switched to lenvatinib when it progressed, and now the lenvatinib is also failing. My hepatitis C was cured with Epclusa years ago, but I still have cirrhosis with some portal hypertension and mild low platelets. I get around fine and drive myself to appointments, though I tire more easily than I used to. I would like a trial within a few hours of New Orleans. My head has never been scanned. I do not know enough about trial phases to prefer one.

I had my gallbladder out for what we thought were gallstones and the pathology showed gallbladder cancer, a type of biliary tract cancer. A second surgery removed part of my liver and the nearby lymph nodes, and the margins were clear with no visible cancer left. I am now taking capecitabine pills for six months as a precaution and have about two months to go. I do not know how that counts as a line of treatment. I also have ulcerative colitis that is flaring at the moment, and I take mesalamine for it. Otherwise I am healthy and active, and I am not pregnant.

My husband is 79 and was told in the spring that he has liver cancer; the doctors talked about a mass and some nodules but I do not know whether it is the hepatocellular kind or a bile duct cancer, and nobody has mentioned any gene tests. He has been taking a cancer pill since June, but I cannot remember the name right now. He has gone downhill fast and is in bed most of the day; I help him to the bathroom and he eats very little. He drank heavily for many years. We have not been told whether he has hepatitis or whether the cancer is anywhere outside the liver.

I am 39 and have been fighting perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (a bile duct cancer) for almost three years; it has spread to the lining of my abdomen and to lymph nodes. I have had gemcitabine and cisplatin, then FOLFOX, and most recently pemigatinib because my tumor has an FGFR2 fusion, but it stopped working this summer. My IDH test was negative. I have a biliary stent and my bilirubin is currently normal. I am tired and need to rest for part of the day, but I still cook and get out of the house. I live in Anchorage and am willing to fly anywhere for an early-phase trial.

I have cirrhosis from fatty liver disease (I never drank and have no hepatitis) and a hepatocellular carcinoma was removed from my liver two years ago. It came back in the same area this year as a single 4 cm tumor, confined to the liver, and I was treated with Y-90 radioembolization in May. The follow-up MRI shows the tumor is still alive at the edges. I have not had any chemotherapy or immunotherapy pills or infusions yet, so I do not know how to answer the question about lines. I also have atrial fibrillation on apixaban. I am independent, play golf twice a week, and would prefer something close to Fort Worth. I do not have an opinion about phase 1 versus later studies.

I noticed a lump on the side of my neck in July and the biopsy showed squamous cell carcinoma coming from the base of my tongue (oropharynx). The pathology says it is HPV-related (p16 positive), and the PET scan shows the tumor and lymph nodes on that side of the neck but nothing anywhere else. I have not had any treatment yet; the plan is chemotherapy with radiation, but I asked about trials that might reduce the dose of treatment. I quit smoking 20 years ago. I am in good shape, still working in a warehouse and lifting without trouble. I do not know whether PD-L1 was checked. I have never been tested for hepatitis as far as I know, and I do not understand the trial phase question or what measurable disease means.

I had squamous cell cancer of the tongue removed in 2023 with a neck dissection, followed by radiation and weekly cisplatin. This spring it came back in both lungs. The tumor is HPV negative and PD-L1 positive with a CPS of 20. I have been on pembrolizumab with carboplatin and 5-FU since April, now on maintenance pembrolizumab alone, and the last scan showed one of the lung nodules getting larger. I eat through a feeding tube because of swallowing problems from the radiation, but I am otherwise active, drive, and look after my grandchildren two days a week. I am not pregnant. I have not had a brain scan.

I have nasopharyngeal carcinoma, EBV-positive, first treated in 2022 with chemoradiation after induction gemcitabine and cisplatin. In 2024 it spread to my liver and bones and I received gemcitabine and cisplatin again together with toripalimab for about a year. When it progressed I was switched to capecitabine, which I am taking now, but my EBV DNA level keeps rising. I am a carrier of hepatitis B and take entecavir, with normal liver tests. I feel reasonably well, work from home full time, and am happy to travel across the western states. I am not sure whether PD-L1 was ever tested.

I was diagnosed with adenoid cystic carcinoma of the parotid gland in 2016 and had the gland removed with facial nerve sparing, followed by proton radiation. Over the last three years several small nodules have appeared in my lungs and they are slowly growing; my doctors say this is the same cancer and that it tends to be slow. I have never had chemotherapy or any pills for it, so I am not sure how to answer about lines of treatment. No HPV or PD-L1 testing was done as far as I know. I had DCIS of the breast treated with a lumpectomy and radiation in 2014 with no recurrence. I am active, hike regularly, and would travel for the right study.

I am writing on behalf of my father, 83, who was just diagnosed with a cancer in his neck; the biopsy report says carcinoma and the doctor thinks it started somewhere in the throat but we are waiting on more tests. We do not know yet whether it has spread. He has not had any treatment. He is weak, mostly stays in his recliner or bed, and has lost about 20 pounds because swallowing hurts. He has chronic kidney disease and a pacemaker. He cannot travel far from Salina, and we have not heard anything about HPV or other markers.

I am 33, never smoked, and was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the gum (oral cavity) in June. It was removed with part of my jaw and a neck dissection; one margin was close and two lymph nodes were involved. I am now halfway through radiation with weekly cisplatin to lower the chance of it coming back. Scans after surgery show no remaining cancer. The tumor was HPV negative and PD-L1 negative (CPS under 1). I am not sure how to count lines since this is all part of the first treatment. I am managing well, working remotely most days, and I am not pregnant and not planning to be during treatment. I have no idea which trial phase would be appropriate.

I have squamous cell cancer of the larynx that has spread to my lungs and the bones of my spine. I have been through a lot: cisplatin with radiation in 2021, pembrolizumab for eight months, then cetuximab with paclitaxel, and most recently docetaxel. The tumor is HPV negative with a PD-L1 CPS of 5. Last month a small spot was found in my brain and radiation to it is being scheduled. I breathe through a trach and talk with an electrolarynx. I am tired and spend about half the day sitting or lying down, but I can still take care of myself. My HIV has been well controlled for 15 years with an undetectable viral load. I am willing to travel anywhere for a phase 1 study.

Two weeks ago an endoscopy for trouble swallowing and weight loss found an adenocarcinoma at the junction of my esophagus and stomach. The CT shows several liver metastases and some thickening of the lining of my abdomen, so it is stage 4. The biopsy came back HER2 positive (IHC 3+) and PD-L1 positive with a CPS of 5; it is not MSI-high, and I have not heard anything about claudin testing. I have not started treatment; my oncologist mentioned chemotherapy with trastuzumab and pembrolizumab, and I wanted to see if a trial in New York fits. I feel OK, a little weak from eating less, but working and walking to the subway every day. My head has not been scanned. I do not know what trial phase I would want.
