I have adenocarcinoma of the lower esophagus, stage 3, with the tumor growing through the wall and two nearby lymph nodes involved but no distant spread. I am currently getting weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel with radiation (the CROSS approach) and surgery to remove the esophagus is planned for about eight weeks after it finishes. The tumor was HER2 negative and not MSI-high; I was never told a PD-L1 result. I have Barrett's esophagus that was followed for years. I am tolerating treatment well so far, still cooking and walking every morning. I take metformin for diabetes but my kidneys and liver are fine. I do not know what measurable disease means, I have never been tested for hepatitis, and I have no preference about trial phase.

I have squamous cell carcinoma of the mid esophagus with spread to lymph nodes in my chest and a few nodules in my lungs, diagnosed in early 2025. My first treatment was cisplatin and 5-FU together with nivolumab for about nine months, and when it progressed I moved to paclitaxel, which I am on now with mixed results. PD-L1 was positive (TPS 10). HER2 was not tested since I was told it is not relevant for the squamous type, and MSI was normal. I smoked and drank heavily for 30 years but have quit both. I have a stent in my esophagus and eat soft foods, but my energy is decent and I still do yard work. I do not want to travel more than a few hours from Lexington. Nobody has scanned my brain, and I was never tested for hepatitis as far as I know.

I was diagnosed with stomach adenocarcinoma last fall. I had four cycles of FLOT chemotherapy, then a total gastrectomy in March that removed everything with clear margins, and I am now getting the four post-operative cycles of FLOT. Testing showed the tumor was mismatch repair deficient (MSI-high), HER2 negative, and PD-L1 negative; I am not sure about claudin. Because of the MSI result my oncologist mentioned immunotherapy studies for after chemo, which is why I am looking. I have rheumatoid arthritis that has been quiet for years on hydroxychloroquine. I live alone, manage my own meals in small portions, and walk to church on Sundays. I do not think I have ever been tested for hepatitis.

I am 45 with diffuse-type (signet ring) gastric adenocarcinoma that had already spread to the peritoneum when it was found in 2024. I have had FOLFOX with nivolumab, then ramucirumab with paclitaxel, and I am now on trifluridine/tipiracil (Lonsurf) as my third line, with the ascites building up again. The tumor is HER2 negative, PD-L1 CPS below 1, not MSI-high, and claudin 18.2 positive in about 75 percent of cells, so I am looking for claudin-directed or other early-phase trials. My disease is mostly in the abdominal lining and my doctors say there is nothing measurable on scans. I was in a trial of a different drug last year that did not work for me. I am tired and spend part of the day lying down, but I eat small meals and get out for short walks. I will travel anywhere.

My husband is 80 and was just told he has a cancer where the stomach meets the food pipe. We do not know the exact type or whether it has spread; the scan is scheduled for next week. He has not had any treatment. He has lost a lot of weight because he can only swallow liquids, and he is very weak now, in bed most of the day and needing help to get to the bathroom. He has congestive heart failure and his kidneys are not great either. We have not been told about any HER2 or other tests. We are in Fayetteville and could not go far.

I carry a CDH1 mutation and had a total gastrectomy four years ago for hereditary diffuse gastric cancer; the pathology then showed early invasive cancer and we hoped that was the end of it. This year it came back in both ovaries and in my pelvic bones. I have been on FOLFOX with nivolumab since July (PD-L1 CPS 2) and the last scan showed shrinkage. The tumor is HER2 negative, not MSI-high, and claudin 18.2 negative. I feel surprisingly well, I work full time and run a few miles a week. I am not pregnant and I have a 4-year-old at home. I would travel within the Mountain West or to a major center for the right study.

I was diagnosed with uterine serous carcinoma, an aggressive type of endometrial cancer, in April. I had a total hysterectomy with removal of my ovaries and lymph nodes, and the pathology showed the cancer had reached one pelvic node; all of it was removed. The tumor was HER2 positive (3+) and had an abnormal p53; it was not MSI-high and PD-L1 was not checked. I am now getting carboplatin and paclitaxel with trastuzumab as my adjuvant treatment, cycle four of six. My energy is decent between cycles and I am back to my volunteer work. I take a blood pressure pill and that is about it. I do not know enough about trial phases to have a preference.

I was diagnosed last month with squamous cell cancer of the cervix. The PET scan shows the tumor and several pelvic lymph nodes lit up, but nothing above the pelvis, so they are calling it stage IIIC1. The tumor is HPV 16 positive and PD-L1 positive (CPS 10). I have not started treatment yet; the plan is chemoradiation with cisplatin and possibly pembrolizumab. I have HIV that has been undetectable for years on Biktarvy with a good CD4 count. I feel well, I work as a cashier, and I am not pregnant. I would like to stay near El Paso because of my kids. I do not know whether anything else like HER2 or MSI was tested, what measurable disease means, or which trial phase I would want.

I have Lynch syndrome. I had colon cancer removed nine years ago with no recurrence, and in 2022 I was diagnosed with endometrioid endometrial cancer, which was treated with a hysterectomy, pelvic radiation, and carboplatin/paclitaxel. Last year it came back in my lungs. The tumor is mismatch repair deficient (MSI-high), HER2 negative, with normal p53. I do not know whether PD-L1 was tested. I was treated with pembrolizumab for 11 months and when it progressed I started lenvatinib, which I have been on for five months with a lot of blood pressure and appetite problems. I still live independently, garden, and drive. Portland or Seattle would be ideal but I could go farther. I have never had a brain scan.

I am 29 and was diagnosed in May with adenocarcinoma of the cervix that had already spread to lymph nodes above my collarbone and to my lungs. The tumor is HPV 18 positive and PD-L1 positive; it is not MSI-high. I have been getting carboplatin, paclitaxel, bevacizumab and pembrolizumab every three weeks since June, and the last scan showed a good response. I want to know what trials exist for when this stops working, and I am willing to travel anywhere in the country. I have a toddler and I am definitely not pregnant. My energy is good between treatments and I have no other medical problems.

I am writing for my mother, 77. She had bleeding and a biopsy showed cancer in her pelvis, but the doctors are still not certain whether it started in the cervix or the uterus and she sees the gynecologic oncologist next week. We do not know yet whether it has spread. She has not had any treatment. She is very weak, she has been bedbound for most of the past month and needs help with everything, and she also has heart failure and kidney disease. We have not been told about any HPV or other testing. We could only manage somewhere close to Montgomery.

I have uterine carcinosarcoma, which my doctors treat as a high-grade endometrial cancer, diagnosed in 2022 and removed by hysterectomy. It spread to my lungs and liver within a year. I have had carboplatin and paclitaxel, then pembrolizumab with lenvatinib, then doxorubicin, and now the scans show growth again. The tumor is HER2 2+ by immunostain, has an abnormal p53, is not MSI-high, and PD-L1 was negative. I had two brain metastases treated with stereotactic radiation in January and they have been stable since. I get tired easily and rest a good part of the day, but I live on my own and still manage. I am not pregnant. I am very interested in a phase 1 trial, even if it means a long drive or flight.

I was treated for stage IIB squamous cell cervical cancer in 2023 with cisplatin, external radiation and brachytherapy. This summer the cancer came back in the cervix and upper vagina, but the PET scan shows it has not gone anywhere else, and the surgeons are discussing a pelvic exenteration. The tumor is HPV positive and PD-L1 negative. I have lupus that is currently active, with joint pain and a rash, and I take prednisone and hydroxychloroquine. I am otherwise in good shape, working in an office full time. I am not pregnant. I do not know whether other markers were tested, I have never been checked for hepatitis, and I do not have a preference about trial phase.

I am 19 and was diagnosed in August with high-grade osteosarcoma of my right distal femur after months of knee pain that we thought was from basketball. The staging scans, including a chest CT and bone scan, showed no spread. I am in the middle of pre-operative MAP chemotherapy (methotrexate, doxorubicin, cisplatin) and limb-salvage surgery is planned for November. I have not had any gene or biomarker testing that I know of. I am a college freshman, feeling OK between cycles, walking with a brace. My family would travel for a trial, especially if the tumor turns out to have a poor response to chemo. I do not know what measurable disease means, whether I was ever tested for hepatitis, or which trial phase would fit.

I have a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) of the stomach, first removed by surgery in 2017, with a KIT exon 11 mutation. It spread to my liver in 2019 and I have since been on imatinib, then sunitinib, then regorafenib, and I am currently on ripretinib, but the liver tumors are growing again. The tumor was tested for NTRK and was negative. I have no brain involvement. I feel pretty good overall, I am still working part time as a bookkeeper and have no trouble with daily activities. I would travel within the Northeast for a trial.

I had a retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma removed in 2021 along with my left kidney, followed by radiation to the area. It came back in 2023 in the same region with involved lymph nodes nearby, but repeated scans have shown nothing in the lungs or elsewhere. I was treated with doxorubicin for six cycles, then gemcitabine and docetaxel, and the tumor is growing again on the latest scan. NTRK testing was negative. I had hepatitis C that was cured with treatment in 2018 and my liver tests are normal. I work as a mechanic and feel well except for some back pain. I do not know enough about trial phases to have a preference.

I was diagnosed with Ewing sarcoma of the pelvis at 21. I had VDC/IE chemotherapy and radiation to the pelvis and was in remission for about a year. It relapsed last fall in my lungs and in a rib, and I have been on irinotecan and temozolomide since then, but the newest scan shows new lung nodules. I have not had NTRK testing that I know of. There is nothing in my brain. I am tired a lot and spend part of each day resting, but I live independently. I am not pregnant. I am ready to go anywhere in the country for a phase 1 trial.

In June I had an undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, about 11 cm, removed from my left thigh with clear margins, and the chest CT showed no spread. I am now getting post-operative radiation to the thigh, which finishes in three weeks. I have not had chemotherapy and I do not know how my situation counts as a line of treatment. I had a melanoma removed from my back six years ago that never came back. I am retired, walk two miles a day with a slight limp, and have no other serious health problems. No molecular testing was mentioned to me. I have never been tested for hepatitis that I know of.

I have a spindle cell sarcoma of the forearm with an ETV6-NTRK3 fusion, diagnosed in 2022. It was removed and I had doxorubicin and ifosfamide, but it spread to my lungs and one spot in my brain in 2023. The brain metastasis was removed surgically and treated with radiation and has been stable since. I have been taking larotrectinib for 14 months with a great response, but the last two scans show the lung nodules growing again, and my doctor thinks the cancer has developed resistance. I am looking for a next-generation TRK inhibitor trial. I feel well, work full time as a graphic designer, and am not pregnant.

I am writing for my father, 84, who was found to have a large sarcoma in his abdomen last week; the pathologists are still working out which type it is. We do not know whether it has spread; the full scans are pending. He has had no treatment yet. He is very frail, mostly in bed since a fall in the spring, and needs help with most things. He has heart disease with a weak heart pump. We live in Fargo and could not travel far. We know nothing about any gene testing.

I have papillary thyroid cancer, diagnosed in 2019 and treated with total thyroidectomy and two doses of radioactive iodine. In 2023 lung metastases appeared that no longer take up iodine, so I am considered radioiodine refractory. The tumor has a BRAF V600E mutation and was negative for RET and NTRK. I started lenvatinib in early 2024; it worked well for over a year but the lung nodules are now growing again and the blood pressure side effects have been hard. I am a nurse, still working three shifts a week, and feel well overall. I am not pregnant. Cleveland, Pittsburgh or Columbus would all be fine.

I am 38 and had my thyroid removed in February for medullary thyroid cancer. My calcitonin never came down after surgery and a PET scan in July found spots in my liver and several bones. The tumor has a RET M918T mutation (sporadic, not inherited according to the genetic testing). It was negative for BRAF and NTRK. I have not had any drug treatment yet; my endocrinologist is weighing selpercatinib against a clinical trial. Radioactive iodine does not apply to my type, I am told. I feel fine, apart from frequent diarrhea from the calcitonin, and I work full time as a software engineer. I would travel to Chicago, St. Louis or farther. No one has scanned my head.

Three weeks ago I was diagnosed with anaplastic thyroid cancer. The mass in my neck grew very fast, it is pressing on my windpipe, and lymph nodes on both sides of the neck are involved, but the CT of my chest and abdomen did not show spread elsewhere. Rapid molecular testing found a BRAF V600E mutation; RET was negative and I do not think NTRK was tested. I have not started treatment yet; the team is talking about dabrafenib and trametinib and possibly a trial that adds immunotherapy. I am short of breath and hoarse and spend much of the day resting, but I can still get around the house and bathe myself. I am in Baltimore and would go to Philadelphia or D.C. if needed. I do not know my hepatitis status or anything about trial phases.

I have papillary thyroid cancer that was found in 2015 and treated with thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine. It returned in my lungs and spine in 2021 and stopped responding to iodine. Testing showed an ETV6-NTRK3 fusion with no BRAF or RET mutation. I was on lenvatinib for about two years and switched to larotrectinib last year; it helped for a while but a new scan shows the spine lesion growing. I had bladder cancer scraped out five years ago with no recurrence. I have high blood pressure and mild kidney impairment from the lenvatinib, and a slow heart rhythm with a pacemaker. I am independent, drive, and do my own shopping, though I move slowly. Reno, Sacramento or Salt Lake City are all possible. I have no preference about trial phase.

I am 31 and had a total thyroidectomy in January for papillary thyroid cancer with a few involved lymph nodes in the neck, all of which were removed. I received radioactive iodine in March; the post-treatment scan showed uptake only in the thyroid bed and my thyroglobulin has dropped to nearly undetectable, so my doctor says the iodine worked. I take levothyroxine at a suppressive dose and that is my only treatment now; I have not had any chemotherapy or targeted pills and no genetic testing of the tumor was done. I have Hashimoto's thyroiditis, which is obviously no longer relevant since my thyroid is gone, and no other health problems. I am not pregnant but hope to have children in a couple of years. I would rather stay near Albany.

I am writing about my grandmother, who is 85. A lump in her neck grew quickly over the summer and the biopsy says it is thyroid cancer of an aggressive kind, but we have not been told the exact type. We do not know whether it has spread; she is supposed to have more scans. She has had no treatment so far. She is bedridden most of the time now, with trouble swallowing, and needs help with eating and washing. She has a weak heart and takes several pills for it. We have not heard anything about gene tests or radioactive iodine. She cannot travel beyond Savannah.

I have hereditary medullary thyroid cancer from MEN2A with a germline RET C634 mutation; my thyroid was removed in 2010. The cancer has spread to my liver, lungs and bones over the years. I have been on vandetanib, then cabozantinib, and then selpercatinib, which worked for almost three years before the liver tumors started growing again in the spring; I also had radiation to a painful hip metastasis. BRAF and NTRK were negative. There is no brain involvement. I am tired and spend about half the day sitting or lying down because of the diarrhea and weight loss, but I look after myself. I am looking for a phase 1 trial of a next-generation RET drug and will travel anywhere.

I have a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (grade 2, Ki-67 around 8 percent) that started in my small intestine and has spread to my liver; it was found in 2021 and the primary tumor was removed. I was on monthly octreotide injections for about two years, and when the liver tumors grew I had four doses of Lutathera (PRRT), finishing last December. The newest scan shows growth again and my flushing and diarrhea are back. There is nothing in my brain. I am not pregnant. I feel reasonably well and work full time as a librarian. I would travel within the Southeast or to a major neuroendocrine center.

I was diagnosed with adrenocortical carcinoma in 2024 after a 12 cm adrenal tumor was found and removed along with my left kidney; it was making cortisol. Eight months later it came back in my lungs and the surgical bed. I have been on mitotane together with etoposide, doxorubicin and cisplatin (EDP) since January, and after six cycles the lung nodules are still growing. Nothing has been found in my brain. My oncologist says standard options are limited and suggested looking for a trial. I feel fairly well despite the mitotane fog and tiredness, I still work from home and walk daily. I would travel anywhere in the Midwest or East Coast, including for a phase 1 study.

I am writing for my wife, 69, who was diagnosed two weeks ago with an adenocarcinoma in her liver and bones that the doctors say is a cancer of unknown primary; they have done an endoscopy, colonoscopy, mammogram and a PET scan and still cannot find where it started. They have sent the biopsy for a large gene panel but we do not have the results yet. She has not had any treatment. She has been in a lot of pain and spends a good part of the day resting, but she gets up for meals and short walks around the house. She has never been tested for hepatitis as far as we know. We do not know whether anything is in her brain; the PET did not include her head. We would prefer to stay within an hour or so of Roanoke.

I am 28 with a nonseminomatous germ cell tumor of the testicle, diagnosed in 2023 with spread to the lymph nodes behind my abdomen and my lungs. I had the testicle removed, then BEP chemotherapy, then TIP when my tumor markers rose again, and this year I had high-dose chemotherapy with my own stem cells (autologous transplant) twice. My AFP is rising again and there is a new lung nodule. I also had a single brain metastasis that was treated with surgery and radiation last year and has stayed quiet. I am tired and my hearing and nerves in my feet are damaged from the cisplatin, but I live on my own and get around. I will travel anywhere for a phase 1 or 2 trial.
